title: Prokaryotic and Eukaryotic Cells
short: Prokaryotic cells (bacteria and archaea) have no nucleus or membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells have both. All cells have a membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes and DNA.
trouble: Students think prokaryotes have no DNA or no ribosomes because they have no nucleus. Their DNA sits in the cytoplasm, and they have ribosomes like every cell.

blocks.html: In Plant Cells and Animal Cells you compared two kinds of cell that both have a nucleus. Most of the living things on Earth, by number, have cells with no nucleus at all: the bacteria and the archaea.

Prokaryotic cells (bacteria and archaea) have no nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles. Eukaryotic cells (plants, animals, fungi and protists) have both. All cells have a cell membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes and DNA.

blocks.cap: The two basic plans of cells.

blocks.html: "Pro-karyote" means "before the kernel" (the nucleus); "eu-karyote" means "true kernel." Every cell must store instructions (DNA), read them to build proteins (ribosomes), and keep its inside separate from the outside (a membrane around the cytoplasm). Those four features are the minimum kit for life, so every cell has them. Membrane-bound organelles divide a large eukaryotic cell into compartments, so different jobs can run side by side.

blocks.title: Classify a cell
blocks.q: Under an electron microscope, a cell 2 µm long has a cell wall, ribosomes and a loop of DNA, but no nucleus and no mitochondria. What kind of cell is it?
steps: No nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles: prokaryotic.
The small size (2 µm) fits, too.
A cell wall alone does not decide it: plants and fungi have walls, and so do most bacteria.
blocks.a: A prokaryotic cell (a bacterium or an archaeon)

blocks.title: How much bigger?
blocks.q: A typical animal cell is 20 µm across and a bacterium 2 µm long. How many bacteria would fit end to end across the animal cell?

blocks.html: Thinking prokaryotes have no DNA or no ribosomes because they have no nucleus. A nucleus is just a membrane around the DNA. Prokaryotes have DNA, lying in the cytoplasm, and they have ribosomes like every cell; they could not make proteins without them. Quick check: if it is alive and made of cells, it has DNA, ribosomes, cytoplasm and a membrane.
